title: How the Ozone Layer Shields Life From UV
post_title: How the Ozone Layer Shields Life From UV | QuantaTale
post_description: What the ozone layer does, how CFCs damaged it and what the Antarctic ozone hole is, from NASA and NOAA. Sources: National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/earth/explore/nasa-knows-the-ozone-hole/ and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration https://gml.noaa.gov/ozwv/faq_cat-2.html #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: What shields life on Earth from the Sun's most harmful ultraviolet rays? A thin layer of ozone acts as a sunscreen for the whole planet. Its job is absorbing UV-B, the most harmful ultraviolet radiation reaching the surface. It sits high in the atmosphere, in a layer called the stratosphere. In the 1970s, scientists found that man-made CFC chemicals were destroying it. A single chlorine atom can destroy ozone molecules over and over again. The so-called hole is really a thin patch of depleted ozone over Antarctica. Because CFCs linger in the air, they will keep affecting the ozone layer well into this century.
